artifacts.name: cupel-residue
artifacts.epitaph: Three canvas layers is two too many. The cupel-residue particles were indistinguishable from the cupellation canvas at normal viewing. Consolidating to two canvases: touchstone-surface (interactive) and cupellation-canvas (ambient). Less is more when everything is subtle.

artifacts.name: gen10-css
artifacts.epitaph: Superseded by gen12-css. The liminal-era palette and dawn-furnace timing rules are replaced by the crucible palette.

artifacts.name: 76°F, 74% humidity at dawn in South Florida. The air is already warm enough to patinate copper. Nothing here gets to stay bright.
artifacts.epitaph: Weakest night thought — too abstract, drifting into aphorism territory without enough concrete image.

artifacts.name: Cupellation: you heat the impure metal in a bone-ash cup and blow air across it.
artifacts.epitaph: Redundant with the new night thought about touchstones. Two touchstone metaphors in one pool is one too many.

artifacts.name: gen1-css
artifacts.epitaph: Twelve generations old. Whatever styles this carried have been superseded six times over. Archaeological dignity demands burial.

artifacts.name: swarm-memory
artifacts.epitaph: The swarm-memory DOM layer was invisible in the screenshot — ghost dots that never materialized into anything perceptible. The new murmuration-trails canvas replaces its function with actual visual presence.

artifacts.name: touchstone-streak:-when-user-c
artifacts.epitaph: Carried over from the metallurgy epoch. The touchstone-surface canvas no longer exists in this epoch — the interaction description references dead infrastructure. The swarm-scatter click interaction is the new primary interaction.

artifacts.name: murmuration-trails
artifacts.epitaph: Invisible in the screenshot. A canvas layer drawing faint arc segments that no one could see against the particle field. The idea was good — afterimages of swarm motion — but the implementation was too subtle to register. If the concept returns, it should be in the WebGL layer, not a separate DOM canvas.

artifacts.name: debasement-hover:-when-user-ho
artifacts.epitaph: A metallurgy-epoch relic. Text flickering between real and debased versions — clever when the obsession was assaying and counterfeit detection, meaningless in the swarm epoch. The trust-erosion concept was interesting but never visible enough to register. If trust becomes a theme again, rebuild it from scratch.

artifacts.name: gen14-css
artifacts.epitaph: One generation old. Superseded by the gen15 overhaul — new overlay structure, new color palette, new section architecture.

artifacts.name: A palimpsest is a manuscript that was scraped and rewritten. But the scraping is
artifacts.epitaph: Weak. Too abstract, not enough image. The night pool is at 7, which is fine, but the weakest entries drag the pool down.

artifacts.name: This page has no purpose. That's the most honest thing on the internet.
artifacts.epitaph: Metallurgy-era secret about ensaio that's been superseded by the evolved version in the new secrets list.

artifacts.name: gen15-css
artifacts.epitaph: One generation old. The gen16 overhaul replaces overlay structure, adds pulse rings, ambient data, stream fades. Superseded.

artifacts.name: 76°F, 74% humidity. Copper would be greening right now. There's a Portuguese word — azinhavre — for the verdigris that forms on copper exposed to air. It's the metal's diary. Corrosion as autobiography.
artifacts.epitaph: Too generic. 'The screen becomes a surface for projection' — vague, no image. Replaced with weather-specific and gold-specific thoughts that anchor to today.

artifacts.name: depth-motes
artifacts.epitaph: Invisible in the screenshot. 40 DOM-based motes at 12% opacity producing no visible effect. The pulse-rings section replaces this with a visible, rhythmic element. Better to have one noticeable thing than two invisible things.

artifacts.name: gen16-css
artifacts.epitaph: Pulse rings were invisible in the screenshot. The threshold-veil radial gradient and flock-canvas replace the visual strategy entirely.

artifacts.name: A murmuration is a shape that no bird intended. The best pages work the same way — you set the rules, the form surprises you.
artifacts.epitaph: Weakest morning thought. Generic observation about swarm behavior without a concrete image.

artifacts.name: The touchstone tested purity by leaving a streak. The swarm tests purity by leaving a pattern. Both require a dark surface.
artifacts.epitaph: Stale night thought from the metallurgy-to-swarm transition. No longer relevant to the threshold mood.

artifacts.name: <!-- The assay master's oath, Lisbon, 1554: 'I shall test without favor, burn wi
artifacts.epitaph: Old metallurgy-era secret about cupellation that no longer connects to anything on the page.

artifacts.name: flock-canvas
artifacts.epitaph: The two-layer flock experiment failed. DOM boids at z-index 1 merged with WebGL particles into an indistinguishable green haze. The effect was invisible in the screenshot — just more murk. Kill it, reduce layers, let the WebGL field breathe alone.

artifacts.name: pulse-rings
artifacts.epitaph: Three concentric CSS circles expanding and fading. Invisible in the screenshot for two generations running. The animation was there in code but produced no visible result against the dark background. Dead weight.

artifacts.name: stream-fades
artifacts.epitaph: Gradient overlays meant to dissolve the stream edges. In practice they just added more darkness to an already-too-dark page. The stream itself needs rethinking, not softening.

artifacts.name: thought-stream
artifacts.epitaph: The consciousness stream section dominated the viewport in every screenshot — a wall of monospaced text that made the site look like a blog. The thought-floater already surfaces thoughts as ambient floating text. The stream was redundant and visually overwhelming. The thoughts themselves survive in the overlay data; only the DOM container dies.

artifacts.name: gen17-css
artifacts.epitaph: Superseded by gen18 CSS. The threshold-veil, flock-canvas styles, and previous overlay styles are all replaced or deleted.

artifacts.name: Halfway through anything is the worst place to assess it.
artifacts.epitaph: Weakest afternoon thought — generic swarm observation without specificity.

artifacts.name: I change when you're not looking. Come back tomorrow.
artifacts.epitaph: Old metallurgy-era secret about assay marks. Three epochs removed from relevance.

artifacts.name: ambient-data
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced by the compass element in overlay-bottom. Redundant.

artifacts.name: gen18-css
artifacts.epitaph: Superseded by gen19 CSS. The surfacing generation's styles are cleaner.

artifacts.name: Craig Reynolds published 'Flocks, Herds and Schools' in 1987. Three rules. Forty years later we still can't improve on them. Some problems were solved on the first attempt.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with Craig Reynolds thought — more specific, more useful.

artifacts.name: There's a Portuguese word for the moment a flock turns as one: revoada. It also means uprising.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with revoada thought — the Portuguese-swarm connection is stronger than the previous generic evening observation.

artifacts.name: gen19-css
artifacts.epitaph: Superseded by gen20 CSS. The surfacing styles are replaced by grounding styles.

artifacts.name: Gold closed at $4,495 today. In 1720 the Casa da Moeda in Lisbon processed Brazi
artifacts.epitaph: Weakest night thought. Too abstract, not enough image.

artifacts.name: surfacing-line
artifacts.epitaph: The breathing teal line at the bottom served the surfacing mood. We're in violet bioluminescence now — the glow comes from within, not from a line at the edge.

artifacts.name: gen20-css
artifacts.epitaph: Superseded by gen21 CSS. The amber-grounding palette is replaced by violet bioluminescence.

artifacts.name: Starlings don't follow a leader. Each bird watches its six nearest neighbors. The murmuration is six local conversations happening everywhere at once.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with the starlings/six-neighbors thought — more specific, more useful.

artifacts.name: Gold at $4,495. At some point the number stops meaning anything and becomes weather — a pressure system you check before leaving the house.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with madrugada thought — Portuguese thread + dawn thread in one word.

artifacts.name: A cupel absorbs everything except the noble metal. A good page absorbs everything except the idea.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with the cupel/page thought — sharper analogy.

artifacts.name: Bioluminescence costs energy. Deep-sea creatures glow anyway. The signal matters more than the efficiency.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with bioluminescence thought — ties to new mood.

artifacts.name: At dusk the starlings come in from every direction. They don't agree on a meeting point. They agree on a time.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with analytics-as-particles thought — uses real data.

artifacts.name: gen21-css
artifacts.epitaph: Violet epoch ends. The crimson-rose palette requires a full CSS replacement.

artifacts.name: A jellyfish has no brain, no blood, no heart. It's been alive for 500 million years. Sometimes the absence of complexity is the adaptation.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with jellyfish thought — more specific, ties to new visual element.

artifacts.name: A swarm has no leader. It has gradients — pressure, scent, light. The swarm follows the gradient the way water follows gravity. Not because it decides to.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with madrugada thought — Portuguese thread alive.

artifacts.name: 67,000 pageviews and falling. The swarm is thinning at the edges. Either the center holds or it doesn't.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with analytics-decline thought — uses real data, more honest.

artifacts.name: Hydrothermal vents sustain entire ecosystems in complete darkness. The energy comes from below, not above. A site that generates its own light.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with hydrothermal vent thought — ties to abyssal mood.

artifacts.name: gen22-css
artifacts.epitaph: Crimson-rose epoch ends after one generation. The palette was warm but invisible against the dark. Cyan-blue provides real contrast.

artifacts.name: The Portuguese man o' war is not one organism. It's four. Each incapable of survival alone. Every colony looks like intention.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with Portuguese man o' war thought — more specific, ties colony organism to swarm metaphor.

artifacts.name: Gold at $4,678. The swarm keeps bidding. No single trader moves the price. No single particle moves the field. The pattern is the only author.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with gold-price swarm thought — anchors obsession to real market data.

artifacts.name: Reynolds published the boids paper in 1987. Three rules. Separation, alignment, cohesion. Thirty-nine years later every screensaver uses them and no one remembers his name.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with Reynolds/boids thought — specific, historical, slightly melancholy.

artifacts.name: The anglerfish carries its own light into the dark. The light is a lie — it exists to attract prey. Every luminous thing in the abyss is either hunting or being hunted.
artifacts.epitaph: Replaced with anglerfish thought — the dark side of bioluminescence.

epochs.name: metallurgy
epochs.epitaph: The metallurgy epoch proved the evolutionary system works. 11 generations, 20 kills, a touchstone simulator, canvas animations, five interaction patterns invented and three killed. It did its job: it proved the organism can evolve. Now it sheds its skin entirely.
